risks: Files-count criteria are defined over the product diff (`'~(.legion | docs/solutions)'` as one fileset expression; two positional `~` arguments are unioned and exclude nothing). The raw Files changed tab shows .legion/*.json from the planner's own handoff commit onward; a reviewer reading the spec's `Check` sentence literally could request changes on a passing PR. Check naming: spec names workflows (`ci`, `fail-on-demand`); `gh pr checks` lists jobs (`check`, `gate`). Cite runs by `gh run list` workflow name and run id. Both workflows run on push and pull_request, so a settled head has four runs; `gh pr checks` exits 8 while any is pending, and push-event duplicates can queue for minutes.
`.fail-me` must never be added to the branch: fail-on-demand fails any head where it exists (verified absent on main today).
The `legion gh` grant lives 60 seconds per bash call: run `gh run watch` as a single bash call rather than a polling loop; a 403 after a minute is the grant, not the credential.

Every ledger commit (implement.json, test.json, review.json, the deletion) moves the PR head: each role re-cites CI and the E2E head SHA at the head it actually verified; do not rebase to refresh CI (rebase only on GitHub `CONFLICTING`, and a fingerprint-unchanged rebase is a confirmation, not a round).
